obtained.how: agency PDFs from MDIFW's own server (www1.maine.gov with the folder in lower case; www.maine.gov refuses scripts): the 2026 law book, and the 2023 and 2019 editions the citation also names (saved as MDIFW_2026.2023.pdf/.txt and MDIFW_2026.2019.pdf/.txt)

bibliography.checked_against: the covers of the 2026, 2023 and 2019 editions
bibliography.corrections: The title is 'Maine Inland Fishing Laws 2026' (Maine Department of Inland Fisheries & Wildlife; 'not valid after December 31, 2026'), not 'Maine open-water and ice fishing law book'. The Hot Brook entry is on p. 23 (PDF p. 29). Working URLs: 2026 https://www1.maine.gov/ifw/docs/25-MDIFW-23-FISHING-LAWBOOK-2026.pdf ; 2023 https://www1.maine.gov/ifw/docs/22-MDIFW-6-FISHING-LAWBOOK-2023.pdf ; 2019 https://www1.maine.gov/ifw/docs/2019_MaineFishingLaws.pdf

claims.claim: the fishing law lists the waters under Bancroft, Danforth, T8 R3 NBPP and T8 R4 NBPP; South fishing zone
claims.location: p. 23 (PDF p. 29), Special Fishing Laws, 'Hot Brook Lakes, Lower and Upper'
claims.quote: Bancroft, Danforth, T8 R3 NBPP, T8 R4 NBPP (South Zone)
claims.conditions: 2026 edition; the 2023 edition reads the same; the 2019 edition reads '(South Region)'

claims.claim: the 2019, 2023 and 2026 law books read: 'General fishing laws apply, except: Daily bag limit on white perch: 25 fish. All bass must be released alive at once'
claims.location: p. 23 (PDF p. 29) of the 2026 edition; the same entry in the 2023 and 2019 editions (MDIFW_2026.2023.txt, MDIFW_2026.2019.txt)
claims.quote: Daily bag limit on white perch: 25 fish. All bass must be released
claims.conditions: the bass rule and the white perch limit apply all year (they are not inside the October–December clause)
claims.note: All three editions carry the identical text.

claims.claim: artificial lures only, and trout, salmon and togue released, from 1 October to 31 December
claims.location: p. 23 (PDF p. 29), Hot Brook entry; codes on PDF p. 3 (front flap: Special Law Codes)
claims.conditions: ALO = 'Artificial lures only'; S-7 = 'All trout, landlocked salmon, and togue caught must be released alive at once'

claims.claim: on one reading of the 2026 law book the South Zone general law keeps the lakes open all year, so ice fishing is legal
claims.location: PDF p. 3 (General Fishing Laws, Seasons, Lakes & Ponds, South Zone) with the Hot Brook entry, p. 23 (PDF p. 29)
claims.quote: From Jan 1 to Dec 31: Open to ice and open water fishing.
claims.conditions: South Zone lakes and ponds; the Hot Brook entry carries no 'CI' (closed to ice fishing) or other season code, so the general law applies
claims.note: Read on the page image (PDF p. 3) to be sure of the column: the line is in the Lakes & Ponds column, South Zone row. It is the plain reading, not one of several; the hedge 'on one reading' can go.

claims.claim: Upper exceeds the 500-acre minimum for weigh-in bass tournaments (MDIFW 2019)
claims.note: Not a claim on this entry: 'MDIFW 2019' in §2.7 is the Black Bass Technical Work Group slides (ledger key MDIFW_2019); show.mjs matched it here because this entry names a 2019 edition. The law book has no tournament rule (searched 'tournament' and '500 acres' in the 2026 edition: no hits). Nothing else in §2.7 is taken from the law book.

tried.note: an all-lower-case file name does not exist; only the folder needs lower case

notes: Every regulation the paper quotes is right in all three editions (2019, 2023, 2026). Only the title needs fixing, and §2.5's hedge on ice fishing can be dropped: South Zone lakes and ponds are open to ice and open-water fishing all year, and the Hot Brook entry has no code that closes ice fishing. The South Zone general bass limit (2 fish, only 1 over 14 in) is overridden here by the release-all-bass rule. §2.7's 'MDIFW 2019' belongs to MDIFW_2019, not to this entry.
